What this volume contains

The fifth volume covers the Level B2 Operating competence: approx. 600 hours of study, from the week 157 to 253 of the calendar. Presumption of Level B1 after: use the verbal forms I/X, the liabilities and the maṣdar, read short, no-vocal news with the root dictionary, write abstracts and formal letters, converse on familiar and topical themes, and you'll get it in Egyptian in everyday life.

No Anki deck and no Excel file. Like the Volume 4, this volume is only the PDF. Flashcards are replaced, in each unit, by the active call-back section ('Return'). Who wants a deck can create it from Appendix B, which contains all the vocabulary with root, category and notes; the progress log shall be kept on a notebook or personal spreadsheet.
Level Objectives B2
At the end of the level:
1. autonomously read authentic articles without vowels 400–600 words (cronaca, politics, economy, law, opinion), with a method and with the dictionary only as last instrument;
2. read in silence an article without vowels at least 90 words per minute and report content, sources and positions;
3. recognize who says what, with what degree of certainty and with what connotation; distinguish facts, interpretations and opinions;
4. understand interviews, news and debates at normal speed, even when the speaker passes from fuṣḥā to dialect; write a dictation with at least the 90% correct words;
5. translate an entire article into English while maintaining attribution, certainty and register (Accessibility at least
3/4), and in Arabic a simple news without casts;
6. write an argumentative text of about 300 words and a neutral summary of a debate of about 150 words;
7. expose for five minutes a topic in fuṣḥā spoken, answered the objections, participated in a discussion and report a report with precision;
8. in Egyptian stories, comments on current affairs, shops, write messages and move to the register read in a meeting;
9. recognize the great dialectal areas, follow broad lines a Levantine debate and a conversation in darija Moroccan, read the written dialect and the Arabic;

10. analyze an article from open sources and write a report; conduct an informative interview and make a Faithful account (INT track). These are internal objectives of the course, written on the model of the descriptors of the Common European Framework for Level B2. Passing the exam B2 does not amount to CEFR certification (see "Seals and Evaluation").

blocks.text: The traces of variety

EGY-11 EGY-18 (weeks 157–226). The Egyptian chosen in A2-24 becomes a language of work and relationship: telling and reporting speeches, commenting on current affairs and following a talk show, solving practical problems and negotiating, conducting and understanding interviews, humor and proverbs, writing messages, greetings and condolences, understanding podcasts and documentaries, and finally reading the register of presentations and meetings. EGY-18 closes the track with an Egyptian profile; Afterwards, the Egyptian remains active with an hour of review per week and with the Egyptian passage of each test and exam. ARZ-01 and ARZ-02 (weeks 199–208). The Arabic (Arabic in Latin characters, with numbers instead of some letters) and the dialect written on social media: messages, comments, posts, Egyptian graphics and with a look at the Levant and the Gulf. MAG-01 MAG-04 (weeks 227–252). The Moroccan (darija) of Fès, only for understanding: sounds, greetings and verb; Numbers, prices and loans; family and hospitality; The media darija and the written one. It is the second variety of the course, chosen because it is among the most distant from fuṣḥā and from the Egyptian and because many Moroccan speakers live in Italy. The MAG units do not ask to speak Moroccan: they ask to understand and respond with courtesy formulas. The Levantino and the other areas. Levantine is studied passively in unity B2-18 (talk shows and debates) and returns to the test and exam ratings; B2-21 teaches to recognize the great areas (Egypt, Levant, Iraq, Gulf, Tunisia, Morocco) with a table of traits and a prudent method. Who reads the scripts. The dialect scripts should be read by speakers of that variety (tutor, tandem partners, friends): vocal synthesis does not pronounce dialects reliably. Prudence. Recognizing a variety means formulating a linguistic hypothesis about how a person speaks, not deducing his nationality, origin or opinions (B2-21).
The INT track

INT-03 → INT-06 continue the specialist module started in B1: the language of diplomacy (verticals, communications, joint declarations), humanitarian crises in news, disinformation and verification, rhetoric of public speeches. B2-23 closes the track of the level with two complete exercises: INT-A , written analysis of an article from open sources with a report in English and a summary in Arabic; INT-B, an informative interview with his report. Track rules apply throughout the course: only open and public sources; no search for information on private citizens; no false identities and no access to non-public spaces; security issues and conflicts treated only as a vocabulary of news; invented cases; no operational procedures. The track teaches a linguistic method (who says what, with what certainty, with which words), does not replace vocational training or the rules of service belonging to it.
Conventions

Transcription. The DIN system is used 31635, as in previous volumes. For the Egyptian: g per ⁧ج⁩ , ʾ for the ⁧ق⁩ pronounced as hamza, ē and ō for long vowels born from ay and aw. For Moroccan: ə for the short indistinct vowel, ž for ⁧ج⁩ , the same signs for the emphasis (ṭ, ḍ, ṣ). Vowels. The B2 is the level of reading without voice:

Dialogues. In standard Arabic units, dialogues have two columns (Arabic and translation); transliteration remains in vocabulary and pronunciation. In EGY and MAG units, dialogues have three columns (dialect, transliteration, translation); in ARZ units the messages have three columns (Arabic, Arabic, Translation). Symbols. ★ in the vocabulary indicates a high frequency word to be used actively. ⁧◌⁩ indicates a space to be completed. " (Recognize) " means a form to be understood but not yet to be produced. Arabic and Italian on the same line. Arabic can be read from right to left even inside an Italian sentence. When multiple Arabic words are separated only by spaces or punctuation, the layout sets them as a single Arabic phrase; where they are separated by ...................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... In the tables, all cells in Arabic are aligned to the right. Invented texts. News, speeches, interviews and debates of the book are invented and serve only for didactic purposes, even when imitating the style of the real press. In order not to confuse exercises and current events , the countries and news organizations are imaginary: the Republic of the Sea , the Kingdom of Oasis , the Organization of the States of the Basin . newspapers - al-Ufuq al-ʿArabī» ( ⁧الأفق العربي⁩ ) e «al-Masāʾ al-Ǧadīd» ( ⁧المساء الجديد⁩ ) are invented. The people mentioned in the texts are invented; no example attributes words or deeds to real people. When a text contains real information (a city, an institution, a historical data), the text or the solution says so.
Method

The standard week (standard rhythm, 60–75 minutes a day): 10 minutes of active booster review, 30–40 lessons and exercises, 20–25 authentic reading or listening; in two of the seven days, instead of the standard Arabic lesson, a block of 40–45 minutes of the variety trace. In addition, one or two sessions a week with the tutor. At a light pace every week of the calendar lasts two real weeks; At an intensive pace, extra time goes into authentic texts and conversation, not in anticipating unity. How a unit is made. Standard Arabic units have a card (code, level, prerequisites, time, materials, targets, day-to-day plan) and 20–21 sections: two dialogues, explanations with tables, pronunciation, new vocabulary with root, category, genre and plural, examples in context, graduated exercises, two readings without vowels, a translation with the column, writing, listening (with dictation), oral production, errors typical of italophones, review to active recall, final verification and criteria to move to the next unit. INT units have the same structure in two weeks. EGY units have 16 sections, ARZ and MAG units 13–14, focused on recognition. Authentic texts. From B2 units ask for a real text every week: an article from an Arabic newspaper, a news outlet, a talk show, an official speech, an Egyptian podcast. Appendix C indicates where to find them. Choose public and reliable sources, record tested and date, and apply the reading method (B2-01) and verification (INT-05). I'm going back without Anki. The active callback review is an Italian → Arabic table: cover the right column, answer aloud, then check. Redo the table of the previous unit at the beginning of each new unit, and those of the weak units in the bearing weeks. Exercises and solutions. Always answer in writing before looking at the solutions. In tutor mode the exercises arrive one at a time and the solution is not shown before your answer, except your request. I'm listening. The course does not contain audio recordings. Each listener has a script: ask another person to read it, or paste the scripts into fuṣḥā in an Arabic vocal synthesis app, without reading them first. Voice synthesis can make mistakes in vowels, endings and some consonants: the pronunciation of reference is that of the tutor. The scripts in dialect should be read by speakers. Alongside the scripts, listening to authentic transmissions is part of the program (Appendix C). The dictionary (by root, Arabic monolingual for control, Italian for surrender) is the instrument of translation. In the tests and exams it is only allowed in the translation tests.

Stories. The criteria in the tests range from 1 a 4; in the examination by 1 a 5 by writing and oral, by 1 a 4 for translation. The translation to Italian has two criteria (Accuracy and Return in English), that towards Arabic two (Accuracy and Correctness of Arabic). Neutral synthesis has its own criterion, fidelity and neutrality. The pronunciation, interaction and registry evaluates them as a native language tutor: without tutor the oral part remains open and does not replace with a self-assessment. What does a passed exam say? The exams of the course are self-correct or correct by the tutor: they attest that you have mastered the studied program, not that you possess a certified CEFR level. The end of the B2 is the right time for external feedback in front of an independent examiner: the possibilities with verified information are in Appendix C.

Studying with the tutor
For a guided session, write "Session" followed by the unit code (e.g. "Session" B2-09EGY Session-14MAG- Session02() and paste the last line of the register. The session always follows the same steps:
1. short recovery of the previous unit;
2. 3–5 quick questions about what you should already know;
3. explanation of the new topic with examples;
4. exercises one at a time, with the solution only after your answer;
5. correction with cause of error and a consolidation exercise;
6. updated log line and targeted review for the following days.

In B2 serve 1–2 sessions per week with a native speaker teacher, even online, and if possible an Egyptian tandem partner: for conversation, exhibitions, correction of translations and argumentative texts, script reading and oral tests and exams. The MAG track serves at least a few sessions with a Moroccan speaker; for the listenings levantini, with a Levantine speaker.
The progress log

Keep the log on a notebook or spreadsheet of your own, with one line per week. Recommended columns: date, calendar week, standard Arabic units, units of variety, unit verification score, scores per part of the tests, address book criteria, words per minute of timed reading, percentage of dictation, authentic texts read or listened to (head and date), study time, notes on errors. It is the source of truth of your path, independent from any platform memory, and it is the basis of the profile by skill of B2-24.
